Below is a rundown of the major quarterly reports expected during the week of October 12–16.
The week starts off relatively quiet, as there are no major earnings announcements planned.
is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Tuesday, October 13, following a strong second quarter and upbeat management commentary on trading and investment banking activity.

In Q2 2026, JPMorgan reported net income of $21.2B and EPS of $7.70, well above the $5.59 consensus, while managed revenue rose 27.7% Y/Y to $58.0B. Results included a $7.9B gain from the sale of Visa shares and a partial release of credit loss reserves. Excluding these items, EPS was $6.14, and return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) reached 23%. Following the quarter, management raised its full-year 2026 guidance for net interest income (NII) excluding Markets to approximately $96.5B, total NII to $105.5B, and adjusted expenses to $107.5B, while lowering its expected card net charge-off rate to approximately 3.2%.

JPMorgan’s Q3 outlook has strengthened following comments from head of trading Troy Rohrbaugh in September that trading revenue and investment banking fees could each increase by a mid-to-high teens percentage Y/Y. This contrasts with Bank of America’s forecast for a decline of more than 10% in investment banking fees. On October 7, JPMorgan also announced the expansion of Chase Payroll, powered by Gusto, extending its business banking services for small and midsize businesses.

Barclays maintained an Overweight rating and a $420 price target on October 6, forecasting Q3 operating EPS of $6.02 against consensus of approximately $5.90. The firm also expects JPMorgan to provide an initial 2027 NII forecast of around $103B. Options markets imply a potential move of approximately 4.4% in either direction following the results, above the 10-year average earnings-day move of 3.4%.
Wall Street rates JPMorgan a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating is more cautious at Hold.
JPMorgan has beaten revenue and EPS estimates in 7 of its past 8 quarters.

is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Tuesday, with recent pipeline developments across oncology, immunology, and neuroscience adding to the focus on its pharmaceutical growth outlook.

In Q2 2026, Johnson & Johnson reported record revenue of $25.31B, up 6.6% Y/Y, while adjusted EPS of $2.90 topped the $2.84 consensus. Innovative Medicine sales reached $16.4B, up 7.8% operationally, supported by oncology drugs DARZALEX, CARVYKTI, ERLEADA, and RYBREVANT, while SPRAVATO sales rose 40.8% in Neuroscience. MedTech revenue increased 4.5% operationally to $8.9B. Following the results, management raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance midpoint to $101.1B and lifted adjusted EPS guidance to $11.60-$11.75.

Recent clinical developments have added to the company's pipeline momentum. Five-year CARVYKTI data showed treatment-free remission in 50% of patients with early-line relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. TREMFYA also met its primary and major secondary endpoints in the Phase 4 STAR study, while CAPLYTA reported positive Phase 3 results for depressive episodes associated with bipolar disorder. These updates reinforce J&J's efforts to expand its oncology, immunology, and neuroscience franchises.

Analyst sentiment remains broadly positive. Guggenheim reiterated a Buy rating and $287 price target on October 7, while RBC Capital raised its target to $290, citing pharmaceutical performance, including TREMFYA and Icotyde. JPMorgan raised its target to $285 from $270 while maintaining a Neutral rating. Talc litigation remains a key legal overhang, including a $1.56B Maryland jury verdict that the company plans to appeal.
Wall Street rates Johnson & Johnson a Buy, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating is more cautious at Hold.
Johnson & Johnson has beaten revenue estimates in each of its past 8 quarters and missed EPS estimates just once over that period.
is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Wednesday, with management's cautious outlook for investment banking fees setting expectations ahead of the release.

In Q2 2026, Bank of America reported net income of $9.1B and diluted EPS of $1.21, topping the $1.13 consensus. Revenue rose 19.6% Y/Y to $31.56B, above estimates of $30.78B. Investment banking fees increased 50% Y/Y, trading revenue rose 33%, and return on tangible common equity reached 17%. Management also pointed to continued net interest income (NII) growth, supported by asset repricing and balance-sheet expansion.

At the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference in September, CEO Brian Moynihan forecast a decline of at least 10% Y/Y in Q3 investment banking fees to $1.6B-$1.8B from approximately $2B a year earlier. Sales and trading revenue was expected to remain roughly flat against the prior-year quarter's $5.4B. The outlook prompted a 5.1% drop in BAC shares, with trading volume 86% above the three-month average. On October 6, JPMorgan analyst Vivek Juneja lowered his Q3 EPS estimate to $1.12 from $1.16 while maintaining an Overweight rating and a $72 price target. MarketBeat's analyst consensus was Moderate Buy, with an average price target of $63.78.
Wall Street rates Bank of America a Buy, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating is more bullish at Strong Buy.
Bank of America has beaten EPS estimates in each of its past 8 quarters and missed revenue estimates just once over that period.

is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the U.S. market opens on Thursday, with record quarterly revenue already indicated by monthly sales data. Attention is likely to center on the cost of ramping up its 2 nm process, margin trends, and the outlook for continued AI-driven demand.

In Q2 2026, TSMC reported revenue of $40.20B, up 36% Y/Y, while EPS of $4.31 beat the $3.82 consensus by 12.8%. Gross margin reached a record 67.7%, operating margin was 60.3%, and net income attributable to shareholders increased 77.4% Y/Y. For Q3, management guided to a revenue of $44.6B-$45.8B, a gross margin of 65%-67%, and an operating margin of 56%-58%, with the anticipated margin decline reflecting the cost of ramping advanced manufacturing nodes. TSMC also raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure outlook to $60B-$64B and increased its revenue growth forecast to above 40% Y/Y from more than 30%.

TSMC's latest monthly sales data point to continued momentum. The company reported Q3 revenue of approximately NT$1.49T, up about 39% Y/Y, including September revenue of NT$511.86B, up 54.6%. This puts quarterly sales near the upper end of its guidance range. Industry reports have also pointed to rising customer demand for the 2 nm process family, while Bloomberg reported that TSMC was evaluating a potential semiconductor hub in Texas to complement its planned U.S. manufacturing investments. These developments add to the focus on capacity expansion, advanced-node demand, and the investment required to support future growth.

Analyst sentiment remains bullish. Stifel initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $515 price target, while Bernstein reiterated Buy with a $554 target. Morgan Stanley has highlighted the importance of TSMC's 2 nm technology to Apple's upcoming product lineup.
Wall Street maintains a Strong Buy consensus on TSM, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating is more cautious at Hold.
TSMC has beaten EPS and revenue estimates in each of its past 8 quarters.
